title: S(3;5,5,5) = 94
statement: The generalized off-diagonal Schur number S(3;5,5,5) is exactly 94: every 3-colouring of {1,...,94} contains x_1+...+x_{4}=x_5 monochromatic in colour 1, or x_1+...+x_{4}=x_5 monochromatic in colour 2, or x_1+...+x_{4}=x_5 monochromatic in colour 3; and some 3-colouring of {1,...,93} avoids all three.

concept_refs.note: graph/concepts/schur-number.md, authored for this family and committed to math-education as ce3e2a5; verified present at graph_pin ce3e2a52e7c9. The node's body carries this family's central soundness warning -- that when colours forbid DIFFERENT equations they are not interchangeable, and a search assuming otherwise reports no colouring exists when one does.
the additive-Ramsey case; off-diagonal is the analogue of asymmetric Ramsey numbers

provenance.conjectured_by: Ahmed-Schaal Conjecture 2 predicts S(3;s,t,u) = s*t*u - t*u - u - 1 for 4 <= s <= t <= u. This value, 94, AGREES with it. The conjecture is open; arXiv:2604.11030 (Song and Mao, April 2026) proves the companion Conjecture 1 but not this one.

evidence.notes: Found by the CDCL core, then replayed by OffDiagonalSchur::first_violation (independent of the encoder) and cross-checked a second time against the FULL, unreduced solution-set list before being written.

Produced by axeyum's own proof-producing CDCL core (solve_with_drat_proof_streaming, ADR-0381) streaming TEXT DRAT to disk and re-derived in the same process by axeyum's own backward DRAT checker (check_drat_backward, ADR-0382). No external solver and no external checker took part. The deciding CNF is the SUBSUMPTION-MINIMAL encoding: for solution sets S subset of S', clause(S) implies clause(S'), so only the minimal antichain is emitted -- a SUBSET of the full clause list, so refuting it refutes the full instance. check-claim-certificates.py validates the stored CNF clause by clause rather than by byte-identity, which is the check the bound actually needs.

evidence.supports: identifies F_94, the formula the refutation is about
evidence.notes: The deciding instance at n = 94, gzipped. Re-checked CLAUSE BY CLAUSE against the claim's own parameters by check-claim-certificates.py: every negative clause must forbid a genuine monochromatic solution of the equation ITS colour carries, and the structural clauses must be exactly the sound at-least-one / at-most-one / BLOCKED symmetry set. Not by hash alone, and not by byte-identity with a regenerated file -- the encoder legitimately drops subsumed clauses, so clause-wise validity is the property the bound actually needs.

notes: REPRODUCES a published computed value. REPRODUCTION. This value is already published (T. Ahmed); ours agrees exactly and additionally carries a machine-checked refutation, which the published computations do not. Generated by crates/axeyum-search/src/offdiag.rs entry point OffDiagonalSchur::minimal_problem. Both sides are discharged -- n = N-1 satisfiable with an independently replayed colouring, n = N refuted with a DRAT proof re-derived by axeyum's own checker. SOUNDNESS NOTE: colours here are NOT interchangeable (each forbids a different equation), so the usual whole-palette symmetry breaking is UNSOUND and would produce a wrong unsat. The encoding orders colour classes only within blocks of colours carrying the SAME equation, and crates/axeyum-search/tests/offdiag_schur.rs carries a negative control showing the unblocked version turning satisfiable S(3;3,4,5) at n=41 into unsat.
